stories.summary: An EA office building in Madrid was vandalized with the words "Save Mass Effect" just days after the company announced it had shuttered series developer BioWare.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Save Mass Effect Graffiti Reportedly Spray-Painted Outside EA Building
sources.text: An EA office building in Madrid was vandalized with the words "Save Mass Effect" just days after the company announced it had shuttered series developer BioWare. It's the latest update to an ongoing story that started when the beloved sci-fi RPG series was put on an indefinite hold earlier this month. With the studio's Mass Effect: Universe project canceled and the franchise without a future, fans have now seemingly taken their push to see the series continue with spray paint. EA's Madrid office in Spain was seemingly the target of one disgruntled fan hoping to make a change. Reddit user Ok_Link9625 shared pictures of the graffiti in question, which show at least two separate instances of Save Mass Effect being tagged around the location. "I stumbled upon the EA offices in Madrid as I was leaving a movie theater and saw this on the floor to the entrance and on the wall in front of the offices #SaveMassEffect," the post said. #SaveMassEffect is an idea that emerged in the moments after EA put the franchise on hold and laid off BioWare staff, but it didn't take long for it to become more than a social media hashtag. The days following the move saw fans erect a Save Mass Effect petition , which exploded and now stands at 290,000 signatures at the time of this piece's publication. As some fans called to boycott EA products over its decision, others, like the folks at We Are Mass Effect, took their love for the series to the streets of New York. It resulted in perhaps the most famous play for #SaveMassEffect thus far, as citizens in Times Square were treated to a billboard for the movement throughout October 26. The group said it plans to fund more billboards in the near future, including one set to go up outside this year's The Game Awards. I WENT OFFLINE FOR FEW HOURS AND SOMEONE PAINTED A WHOLE GRAFFITI IN FRONT OF EA OFFICE? Graffiti, however, is a new tactic, and it has received pushback in the community. While some want to keep the pressure up not only to breathe life into the franchise but also to support the people who have made it, others have said they aren't sure how tagging office buildings will move the needle. "I'll admit, I'm not sure this is the way to make them think the IP is worth saving," another top reply argued . Mass Effect series composer, meanwhile, simply took the opportunity to recognize how quickly the campaign has evolved in just a few days: "The fans are serious as a heart attack!" We absolutely did not ask people to do this and obviously vandalism is bad, but it's insane to me that #SaveMassEffect is so big that someone in Madrid is this angry. I get it. @heleuscluster Oh shi**, man, we have banksy on our side :D https://t.co/HNHAwdFAtL At the moment, it doesn't look like billboards or graffiti have done much to convince EA to support any angle the movement hopes to achieve. The most recent information about the fallout came from Bloomberg , which reported that the publisher canned its plans to release Mass Effect 5 in favor of prioritizing Star Wars Battlefront 3 . Alleged details about the canceled game promised that BioWare was creating a story that would have accounted for all choices players made in previous installments . sources.text: While evergreen to say that Mass Effect fans are having a rough go, itâs hard to imagine a worse couple of weeks. Its most impassioned players have been incensed, to say the least, as one Reddit user stumbled across incidents of vandalism at one of the publisher’s offices. “I stumbled upon the EA offices in Madrid as I was leaving a movie theater,” posted Reddit user Ok_Link9625 , “saw this on the floor to the entrance and on the wall in front of the offices.” Scrawled in spray paint in front of the Madrid officeâs front gate and along one wall reads “SAVE MASS EFFECT.” Itâs an escalation in efforts to salvage the beloved series from an unceremonious end. stories.title: Input Lag Is So Bad in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 on Nintendo Switch 2 That Players Suffer From a 'Competitive Disadvantage'
stories.summary: If you’re playing Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 on Nintendo Switch 2, beware: you’re at a disadvantage in competitive Multiplayer due to crushing input lag that is much worse than the other platforms.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Input Lag Is So Bad in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 on Nintendo Switch 2 That Players Suffer From a 'Competitive Disadvantage'
sources.text: If you’re playing Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 on Nintendo Switch 2, beware: you’re at a disadvantage in competitive Multiplayer due to crushing input lag that is much worse than the other platforms. Digital Foundry’s analysis of the performance of the Switch 2 version of Modern Warfare 4 — the first Call of Duty released on a Nintendo console since 2013’s Ghosts — found that the input lag on Switch 2 can be two times longer than on PS5 at 60fps. In competitive Multiplayer, Switch 2 aims for 60fps and, according to DF, hits that target most of the time (although some things do cause the frame rate to drop, including looking through the transparent visor of a riot shield). Call of Duty Multiplayer prides itself on rock solid 60fps gameplay, which provides a smooth, responsive experience for those who fuss over their K/D ratio in, for example, 6v6. It’s crucial that all platforms the game is available on offer at least 60fps to provide a level playing field for Multiplayer fans — although the debate about the advantage PC players have over console has dogged Call of Duty since the dawn of crossplay. DF reports that Variable Refresh Rate (VRR) support “helps smooth out” framerate drops on supported displays, although you’ll have a harder time of it in terms of performance playing through portable mode. And then we come to responsiveness. DF’s tests show 81ms in docked mode and 100ms in portable mode, the latter of which is double the PS5’s 49.1. In fact, DF found that Multiplayer in portable mode ranged from 83ms at best to 125ms at worst. DF called this "actually deleterious to performance.” DF seems generally happy with the Switch 2 version, which was handled by port specialist Digital Legends with support from Infinity Ward. But if you’re into Multiplayer, the inescapable fact is you are at a disadvantage. No matter how fast your trigger finger, the Switch 2 will take longer to respond. Outside of Multiplayer it’s a different story. The Campaign runs at 30fps, which was good enough for IGN’s Simon Cardy when he played the Switch 2 version of Modern Warfare 4 . “Granted, the textures are nowhere near as detailed, with flat surfaces and faces smoothed over to give the impression of plasticine versions of the campaign’s characters,” he said. “It's by no means a looker, but considering the reduced horsepower Nintendo’s latest console is working with, the gameplay itself was smooth, running at 30fps at 4K while docked.” “Yes, it's quite a visual downgrade when compared to the likes of PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X, but that comes with the territory,” he continued. “And if you’re solely a Nintendo owner who’s been locked out of Call of Duty for over a decade, you’re getting a version of Modern Warfare 4 that feels every bit as snappy as the series usually is, even if it’s a bit muddier than Nintendo’s own crisp visuals.” Why is Call of Duty releasing on a Nintendo console now, 14 years after the last time? It has to do with Microsoft’s $69 billion acquisition of Activision Blizzard. Back when Microsoft was facing regulatory hurdles, one announcement designed to help convince the powers that be to green light the buyout was a 10-year commitment to bring Call of Duty to Nintendo following the merger. “Microsoft is committed to helping bring more games to more people — however they choose to play,” then Xbox boss Phil Spencer said in December 2022. Four years later, and with the Activision Blizzard buyout done and dusted, Call of Duty is on Switch 2. We’ve got an in-progress Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Walkthrough to help you through the campaign missions, plus All Collectible Note Locations , and all the Code Solutions you’ll need to open every keypad and container. For multiplayer, check out How to Level Up Fast in MW4 and our Essential Multiplayer Tips and Tricks alongside the Best MW4 Settings we recommend you use. DMZ is back, so we’ve got a handy DMZ Beginner’s Guide , too. Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. sources.title: O som de Saros: Criando uma identidade de áudio para Carcosa
sources.text: A Housemarque diz como usou criatividade musical e a tecnologia do PS5 para criar os ambientes sonoros imersivos do jogo de tiro sci-fi. Quando começamos a trabalhar em Saros, sabíamos que tínhamos um desafio interessante à nossa frente. Já havíamos estabelecido uma identidade sonora bem distinta em Returnal, e a Housemarque nos deu uma direção clara desde o início: “Refinar, não Reinventar.” Isso se tornou um princípio importante durante o desenvolvimento. Mantivemos a nossa abordagem de gameplay em primeiro lugar, a nossa ênfase em feedback forte e divertido para os jogadores, o nosso ambiente sonoro imersivo e a nossa ambição para utilizar tecnologias do PS5 como o Áudio 3D Tempest e a resposta tátil do DualSense. Ao mesmo tempo, Saros é um novo IP, com seus próprios personagens, história e tom. Toda faixa de áudio e conteúdo precisava ser único e ajudar a estabelecer o mundo de Carcosa. Logo no início, começamos a procurar elementos que poderiam definir Saros sonoramente. O Eclipse se tornou uma de nossas primeiras âncoras artísticas. É algo central ao mundo e à história do planeta hostil, então começamos experimentar com sua identidade sonora. Uma de nossas descobertas mais úteis veio de uma sessão de gravação usando o instrumento didgeridoo no nosso estúdio. Com processamento criativo, as gravações ficaram épicas e incrivelmente versáteis. Com mais manipulação, passaram a parecer vozes bem graves. Isso eventualmente se tornou a fundação para as vocalizações do Yellow King, e ajudou a definir a paleta sonora de Saros como um todo, com ênfase na influência do Eclipse, do Yellow King e da Corrupção pelo jogo. O trailer de anúncio, que foi a primeira apresentação de Saros ao público, se tornou uma oportunidade para mostrar essa exploração criativa, com destaque para o didgeridoo e muitos outros sons. A ideia de gravar algo e transformar depois em algo mais for do comum se tornou importante para o ambiente sonoro como um todo. Unimos gravações primárias com elementos abstratos e altamente processados, criando sons que pareciam familiares e ao mesmo tempo alienígenas. Alguns sons vieram de lugares bem inesperados. O primeiro inimigo que os jogadores encontram, um drone mecânico maligno, é criado parcialmente de sons gravados em disquetes. O oceano na Yellow Shore foi criado através das gravações de frango sendo frito, marinado e de castanhas sendo batidas em uma panela. O design de som muitas vezes é sobre ouvir o potencial em algo que nunca teve intenção de soar como o que você precisa. A trilha sonora de Sam Slater também traz seu próprio e poderoso vocabulário até Carcosa, unindo vozes distorcidas, sintetizadores, guitarras e texturas experimentais mais obscuras. O nosso objetivo foi permitir que a Música e o Design de Som se misturassem e complementassem um ao outro, ajudando a Corrupção a parecer uma força sobrepujante que se espalhou pelo mundo todo. Grande parte do design de som foi ter certeza que as várias partes de Carcossa tivessem sua própria identidade, mas ainda parecessem conectadas ao mesmo mundo. Queríamos que os jogadores pudessem entender o que estava acontecendo à sua volta pelo som, mesmo quando a tela estava cheia de informações visuais. As vocalizações dos inimigos foram criadas para serem breves, tonais e memoráveis, principalmente para ataques que os jogadores precisam reconhecer rápido o bastante para se esquivar ou absorver com o escudo. Criamos famílias sonoras distintas para inimigos orgânicos, cósmicos e mecânicos. Os inimigos cósmicos em particular, precisavam parecer conectados com influência divina do Yellow King, um som que pode ser tanto ameaçador quanto belo. O canto gutural mongol se tornou parte da fundação básica vocal deles, com mais elementos vocais vindo de cantores e instrumentos como o shakuhachi, aumentando ainda mais a sua beleza. Projéteis foram tratados com o mesmo nível de cuidado. Projéteis Normais, Corrompidos e Nova cada um possuem sua paleta. Projéteis azuis usam texturas elétricas e líquidas, os projéteis amarelos Corrompidos tiram seu som da linguagem baseada no didgeridoo, e os projéteis vermelhos usam mais material tonal derivado de gritos humanos. Esses detalhes podem ser sutis individualmente, mas juntos eles podem fazer o mundo ficar mais coerente e ajudar os jogadores a interpretarem o combate intenso. Ao contrário de outros estúdios, os títulos da Housemarque são conhecidos pela sua rejogabilidade e domínio, com o espetáculo bullet-hell de centenas de projéteis enchendo a tela. Desenvolvemos várias camadas de priorização para os sons mais importantes que permanecem audíveis sem silenciar os outros. Inimigos são priorizados de acordo com fatores como seu grau de ameaça, distância, visibilidade e estado de combate. Seu áudio então é priorizado em diferentes níveis de proeminência, para que possamos gerenciar cuidadosamente quando sons estão competindo pela atenção do jogador. Os projéteis usam uma abordagem similar, agrupados de acordo com seu tipo e proximidade, para que o jogo possa comunicar informação mais importante sem confundir o jogador. O resultado é um mix denso que ainda pode comunicar o que mais importa. Usando a nossa experiência com Returnal, quisemos que Saros utilizasse o áudio 3D e a resposta tátil ainda mais, entregando a experiência de áudio mais imersiva através do Dolby Atmos. Em um jogo tão exigente quanto esse, o Áudio 3D não é apenas sobre a imersão. É outra fonte de informação para o gameplay. Inimigos e projéteis podem se aproximar de cima, de baixo, de trás ou até de fora da tela, e o posicionamento preciso pode fazer toda diferença no combate. O nosso processo vai além de uma simples ativação de Tempest no conteúdo posicional. sources.text: Greetings from the clouds and Exiled Lands. We’ve just launched Dune: Awakening on PlayStation 5, but we’re only getting started. We’re excited to bring two more of our open-world survival adventures to PlayStation 5 in early 2027. Soar the skies in Aloft, then visit the unforgiving Exiled Lands in Conan Exiles Enhanced. After six years of heartfelt development with a team that grew from a small group of friends to the Astrolabe of today, we are ecstatic to reveal that our cozy co-op sandbox survival game in the clouds, Aloft, makes its console debut with Funcom as a publisher on PS5 early 2027. The PS5 version includes all the updates released during the game’s Early Access period on PC, as well as the 1.0 experience, bringing our complete vision of Aloft to life, filled with new content, stories, and so many improvements. Turn floating islands into skyships, build a home among the clouds, and explore a colorful open world alone or with friends. Since launching in Early Access, we have introduced five major content updates to Aloft, featuring new wildlife, puzzles, combat improvements, glider customization, expanded exploration, and much more. Discover lost knowledge, cure fungal corruption, care for your animals, brave hurricanes as you restore the ecosystem and uncover new adventures across the skies. Launching the complete game on PS5 marks an exciting new chapter for us. Aloft has always been a passion project fueled by the unwavering support and love of our community. Reaching this milestone is incredibly exciting, as this will mark a new era for the game – we really hope you will be part of our flight. Both PS4 and PS5 versions will be available to purchase. Buy one version and get the other for free. All your purchased Bazaar items and DLC will also carry over from PS4 to PS5 seamlessly. The Enhanced edition brings improved environments, characters, lighting, and effects, along with a redesigned UI and performance and quality-of-life improvements. sources.title: Suit up as Astro Bot in Rayman Legends Retold
sources.text: After making a cameo in Astro Bot (2024), it is now Rayman’s turn to dress up as the Captain of the Bots. Rayman Legends Retold is coming to PlayStation 5 and PlayStation 5 Pro on December 3, and Astro Bot’s iconic design is featured in the game as an exclusive costume, bringing the iconic platformer pairing full circle after Rayman made a cameo in Astro Bot (2024). The PS5-exclusive Astro Bot costume in Rayman Legends Retold will be available for free on players’ first visit to Victor Velour, the game’s resident tailor, at his costume shop. The outfit is once again a collaboration between Ubisoft Milan, Ubisoft Montpellier, and Team Asobi. We sat down with Guillaume Arvieu, Art and World Director on Rayman Legends Retold, and Quentin Chaillet, Lead Character Artist, to discuss the collaboration, how the costume was created, and the DNA shared by two platforming icons. Talk us through the Astro Bot skin design in Rayman Legends Retold – how did you approach capturing the essence of Astro Bot within your own art style? Chaillet: One of the biggest challenges was bringing Astro Bot’s sleek, futuristic aesthetic into Rayman’s universe. Rayman’s designs traditionally have a more handcrafted, organic feel, so introducing these glossy surfaces, metallic details, and high-tech materials was something quite different from what we’re used to. We wanted to stay as faithful as possible to Astro Bot’s iconic design while making sure it still felt authentically Rayman. That meant carefully adapting the shapes and proportions, especially his large nose, no arms / legs, and his big shoes, which are such recognizable parts of Rayman’s silhouette. The goal was to incorporate as many of Astro Bot’s signature details as possible, from the reflective metallic parts and glowing blue elements to the smooth white surfaces, without losing Rayman’s personality or expressiveness. It was a really interesting exercise in finding the right balance between two very different visual identities and making them feel like they naturally belong together. In your own words, what DNA do Astro Bot and Rayman share? Arvieu: Astro Bot has truly established itself as a major player in the platforming genre, with an identity of its own. What I particularly appreciate is how generous the game is: the richness of its worlds, the creativity of its scenarios, and the constant joy of discovering new gameplay ideas. This is something we also find in Rayman. Both games offer incredibly rich fantasy worlds, filled with diverse biomes that invite players to explore, discover, and experience a sense of wonder. They also place great importance on fluid movement, a variety of interactions, and the joy of mastering the possibilities available to the player. Beyond these similarities, I think our two franchises share, above all, the same spirit. They’re both colorful, creative games that are full of surprises and driven by positive values. They aim to evoke emotions, make people smile, and rekindle that almost instinctive sense of joy we feel when discovering a platformer bursting with ideas. These are games that make you feel good. They remind us that video games can be a wonderful source of joy, wonder, and shared experiences, whatever our age. Why do you think collaborations like this are important? Arvieu: Since the early days of video games, creators have been inspiring one another. An idea, a gameplay mechanic, a character, or an artistic approach can spark new ideas and open up unexpected possibilities. It’s an ongoing exchange that fuels our collective creativity. Collaborations like this make that exchange tangible. They allow us to celebrate the work of other teams, bring together worlds that are close to our hearts, and create moments players might never have imagined otherwise. It’s a virtuous circle: everyone brings their own perspective, ideas, and expertise to the table, and we all grow from the experience. Ultimately, it’s the players who benefit, discovering new encounters and sharing in the joy of seeing their favorite characters come together. Rayman has a long history behind him and holds a special place in the hearts of many players, particularly those who first discovered him on the original PlayStation. Astro Bot, meanwhile, celebrates this legacy while establishing its own identity with a new generation of players. Seeing these two worlds come together is therefore also a way of bringing different generations of players together. It’s a little nod to the history of video games, but also a wonderful illustration of the medium’s ability to reinvent itself and continue to surprise us. Rayman Legends Retold is coming to PS5 and PS5 Pro December 3, 2026. Embark on a bold reimagining of the beloved platformer, with new visuals and a retold story. Play solo or up to 4player couch coop, explore a mysterious new realm, jam through new musical stages, and more.

sources.title: First look inside the Prism Collection, with three new transparent designs for PS5 accessories
sources.text: Peer through DualSense controllers and PS5 console covers with this sleek collection of accessories – pre-orders start on November 10. Get ready to see your PS5 console and DualSense controller in a whole new way. Today, we are pleased to introduce the Prism Collection, featuring three striking transparent designs for DualSense wireless controllers and PS5 console covers: Flare Orange, Emerald Green, and Graphite Gray. The new collection was inspired by our design teams’ interest to bring a transparent appearance to PS5, and give players a closer look into the design and craftsmanship behind our DualSense controllers and PlayStation 5 consoles. From bold Flare Orange to elegant Emerald Green and stylish Graphite Gray, each color is finished with a premium glossy sheen for a sleek and elevated design. The luminous Flare Orange brings a bold and vibrant aesthetic to a PS5 setup. The elegant Emerald Green features a silky green exterior. The classy Graphite Gray presents a refined gray design. The Prism Collection brings a fresh new look to the PS5 console and DualSense controllers. To share more about our creative process behind the new design, here are insights from Leo Cardoso and Satoshi Aoyagi from our Color, Material, and Finish design team. “We know how much our fans have been looking forward to the return of transparent controllers. We wanted to bring back the iconic see-through trend of the late ’90s in a fresh, modern way that complements the PS5’s industrial design.” “The high-gloss clear finish extends across the back of the controller, offering a look at the technology that powers the DualSense controller while maintaining a sleek, monochromatic look. The metallic finish on the middle cover brings the contrasting surfaces together for a premium appearance that feels consistent with the PS5 generation. To complement the futuristic aesthetic, we carefully selected three distinct colors: a vibrant orange that subtly takes on a rosy hue where the transparent material overlaps, a deep hunter green that gains depth through its transparency, and a cool-toned storm gray.” The Prism Collection DualSense wireless controllers will be available globally for a recommended retail price (RRP) of $84.99 USD / ¥12,480 (including tax) / €84.99 / £74.99.* The matching PS5 console covers will be available exclusively directly from PlayStation where available** and in other regions in limited quantities through select retailers for a RRP of $74.99 USD / ¥9,980(including tax) / €74.99 / £64.99.* The Prism Collection launches starting on February 4, 2027. Pre-orders will begin on November 10, 2026 at 10am local time directly from PlayStation (where available) as well as participating retailers. The exact launch date and availability for the accessories may vary by country/region. Starting November 10, 2026 at 7:00am PT / 10:00am ET, players in the U.S. will be able to pre-order the Prism Collection direct from PlayStation through direct.playstation.com. Starting November 10, 2026 at 10:00am local time in the U.K., France, Germany, Austria, Spain, Portugal, Italy, Netherlands, Belgium, and Luxembourg, players will be able to pre-order the Prism Collection direct from PlayStation through playstation.com/store/hardware. *Actual retailer prices and availability may vary . **Regions where ordering directly from PlayStation is available: U.S., U.K., France, Germany, Austria, Belgium, Netherlands, Luxembourg, Spain, Portugal, and Italy.
